file:AUR.booster.json.name: AUR
file:AUR.booster.json.notes:
Payload shroud: CONE (corrected from tangent ogive per user 2026-07-28 -- the real AUR fairing is conical), 2.67 m long, body-diameter base (0.8763 m); cone lateral surface pi*R*slant = 3.72 m^2. Mass 22.5 kg from the Akin ENAE 791 fairing MER M=4.95*A^1.15 (same relation as before, re-evaluated for the cone area; was 31.4 kg on the ogive's 4.98 m^2). Physics effect of ogive->cone wave drag + lighter fairing: -73 km range, -31 km apogee on the max-loft reference flight (~2%). Jettison on the heating criterion (q_dot<1135 W/m^2, exoatmospheric).
Stage-1 length corrected 10.2 m -> 5.0 m (user-sourced): the 10.2 was the all-up-round length entered in the stage-1 field (5.0 + 2.6 S2 + 2.67 fairing ~= 10.3 m whole round, matching the ~7,441 kg AUR launch mass bookkeeping).

file:Al_Hussein.booster.json.name: Al Hussein
file:Al_Hussein.booster.json.notes: Tail fins added 2026-07-28. The R-17/Al Hussein carries four clipped-delta tail fins (the shipped entry predated Thrusty's fin fields, so has_fins was False -- physically wrong). fin_span_m = 0.48 m EXPOSED SEMI-SPAN is SOURCED: astronautix R-17 / Army Recognition give a 1.80 m tip-to-tip fin span; exposed semi-span = (1.80 - 0.84 body)/2 = 0.48 m. fin_root_chord_m 1.5, fin_tip_chord_m 0.65, fin_sweep_deg 55, fin_thickness_m 0.03 are PHOTO-SCALED ESTIMATES from R-17 scale drawings, NOT published measurements -- replace with sourced values if available. Boost-drag effect (fins -> _cd_fins friction+wave): -9.5 km / -3.2% on max range for Al Hussein. n_fins = 4.

file:No-dong.booster.json.name: No-dong
file:No-dong.booster.json.notes: Diameter corrected 0.88 -> 1.32 m 2026-07-28: the real No-dong body is ~1.32-1.35 m (the library's Shahab-3, a No-dong copy, was already 1.32); 0.88 m was the Scud diameter, physically wrong. Tail fins added: four clipped-delta fins, Scud R-17 proportions scaled to the 1.32 m body (span/D, root/D, tip/D, 55deg sweep from the Scud-B entry), PLACEHOLDER per user until sourced No-dong fin dimensions are found. IMPACT: max range falls 996 -> 943 km (diameter) -> 926 km (fins). NOTE the model already under-ranges vs the real ~1300-1500 km; the correct diameter makes that gap larger, which points to under-modeled propellant/Isp -- a separate mass/propulsion issue, NOT to be fixed by keeping a wrong diameter (that would be fitting geometry to a range target).

file:STARS-1.booster.json.name: STARS-1
file:STARS-1.booster.json.source: Strategic Target System (STARS): surplus retired Polaris A3 first and second stages with an Orbus 1a third-stage motor; propellant in the three boosters totals 30,541 lb (13,853 kg); approximately 75,000 lb thrust. U.S. Army SMDC/ARSTRAT, Advanced Hypersonic Weapon Program Environmental Assessment, June 2011, sec. 2.1.2 Launch Vehicle Description and Fig. 2.1.2-1. This file carries two stages where the EA describes three; the stage-level masses, Isp and burn times are not from the EA and their source is not recorded. Grid-fin count and deploy schedule follow the AHW flight-test configuration (METHODS sec. 8.5); source not recorded in this file. Google Drive folder LRHW/CPS/EIS (maintainer's library).

file:AHW.ro.json.name: AHW
file:AHW.ro.json.notes:
Conical glide body, SWERVE heritage (AHW = SWERVE with better TPS and higher glide L/D). This is NOT the C-HGB - they are different systems; the C-HGB is a biconic RV (see C-HGB.ro.json). MASS ~450 kg (same class as SWERVE; AHW reuses the SWERVE airframe with a new heat shield). L/D 1.8 is the expected glide value for this conical glide body -- higher than SWERVE's 0.6 small-wing airframe value and below the HTV-2 waverider (2.6). beta=9,000 kg/m2 = m/(Cd*A) holding Cd*A=0.050 m2 (Cd~0.18 on the 0.283 m2 base); scales with mass, so rescale if mass is revised. These aero numbers are REPRESENTATIVE estimates for a conical glide body, not a published fit (Acton fit only the HTV-2; no comparable public AHW aero fit). NOTE on range: at L/D 1.8 a max-range equilibrium glide from a STARS-class apogee reaches ~6,000 km, well beyond the ~4,023 km (2,500 mi) AHW flight-1 range to Illeginni -- so the documented test range is a WITHIN-ENVELOPE mission target, flown via the pitch program at run time, not a max-glide aerodynamic limit. Do not back L/D out of the test range. glider_beta_entry_kg_m2 = 20 is an Acton-style entry beta_S placeholder (Acton, Science & Global Security 23 (2015): 191-219) affecting only the equilibrium_glide_acton path. Guidance is damped_glide (damped-phugoid, zeta 0.7); under glider_aero_model=polar the glider_LD sets the polar max-L/D (k back-solved in _aero_polar) and the phugoid trims near that alpha*, so the 1.8 is honored. glider_beta_entry_kg_m2 then only matters if switched to equilibrium_glide_acton.

Reentry mode: this object was characterised flying damped_glide; the shipped default is the neutral equilibrium_glide. Select the intended reentry mode in the Reentry-mode dropdown (the glide law is a flight-plan choice, not object hardware).
file:AHW.ro.json.source: Advanced Hypersonic Weapon (U.S. Army/Sandia) - conical glide body of the SWERVE lineage (SWERVE with improved thermal protection). Entry model per Acton, Science & Global Security 23 (2015): 191-219. Distinct from the C-HGB, which is a separate biconic reentry vehicle.

file:C-HGB.ro.json.name: C-HGB
file:C-HGB.ro.json.notes: Reentry mode: this object was characterised flying damped_glide, which is now its shipped default reentry plan. The glide law is a reentry-plan choice (still switchable on the sidebar strip), not object hardware.
file:C-HGB.ro.json.source: MASS 450 kg: adopted from U.S. environmental documentation for the C-HGB flight tests. (1) U.S. Navy, Strategic Systems Programs, Final EA/OEA, Navy Flight Experiment-2 (FE-2), December 2019, sec. 2.5.6: 'a quantity of up to 454 kg (1,000 lb) of tungsten alloy is used for the environmental impact analysis' of the FE-2 payload (Table 2-2 lists the payload's structural materials, tungsten among them). (2) U.S. Army RCCTO/SMDC, Biological Assessment for Hypersonic Flight Test-3 Activities, 22 September 2020, sec. 2.2.1 Launch Vehicle Description: the FT-3 payload 'would weigh approximately 350 kg (750 lb) and would be similar to the recently tested FE-2 payload (U.S. Navy 2019), except that the payload would contain approximately 10% of the tungsten contained on the FE-2 payload (which was 454 kg, or 1,000 lbs).' Maintainer's reading: FE-2 payload 454 kg, FT-3 payload 350 kg, the difference being 90% of the tungsten (about 115 kg); the 450 kg here is the FE-2 (full-tungsten) configuration. GEOMETRY (length 1.5 m, base diameter 0.58 m, nose radius 0.02 m): dimensional draft from image, measured by the maintainer with Thrusty's mensuration tool (image_measure.py) on open-source imagery, May 2026. The image, scale anchor and pixel quantum are not recorded (the tool's provenance stamp did not survive the save). Angles are anchor-free; length and diameter depend on the scale anchor. The image's labelled dimensions were mutually inconsistent; the half-angles plus base diameter were trusted over the labelled total length. beta_kg_m2 = 15000 is a PLACEHOLDER with no public source; glider_LD 2.0 is a representative estimate, not a published fit. Google Drive folder LRHW/CPS/EIS (maintainer's library).

file:HTV-2.ro.json.name: HTV-2
file:HTV-2.ro.json.notes:
DARPA HTV-2 waverider. beta_kg_m2 = 26,000 kg/m^2 is the ZERO-LIFT ballistic coefficient (the canonical convention: the polar reads C_D0 = m/(beta*A)). RE-BASED 2026-07-25 from the previous 13,000 (see below). Acton's GLIDE-trim ballistic coefficient beta_L = 13,000 kg/m^2 (Acton Table 3, 'very similar to modern ICBM RVs') is now DERIVED, not stored: at the max-L/D trim C_D = 2*C_D0, so beta_L = beta_zerolift/2 = 26,000/2 = 13,000 -- reproducing Acton exactly (trajectory._aero_polar / analytic beta_L, METHODS 12.0.3). Before the re-base, the stored 13,000 was Acton's glide beta_L mis-read by the polar as zero-lift, giving an implausible C_D0=0.27 and operating C_L*=1.4 (past stall); the re-base gives C_D0=0.14, C_L*=0.71. Trajectory range changed <1% (equilibrium glide is L/D-dominated); this is a correctness/consistency fix, not a behaviour change. L/D = 2.6 (Acton Table 3). mass = 1000 kg (Wright, companion article). diameter_m is the FRONTAL (drag) diameter used for boost-phase reference area, NOT the planform width: Acton models the body as a flat isosceles triangle ~5 m long x ~2 m wide, but flying nose-first the frontal extent is small, so ~0.6 m is a representative frontal-equivalent. The 2 m planform / lifting behaviour is carried by glider_LD, not by this diameter. glider_beta_entry_kg_m2 = 7.0 is Acton's Table 3 fitted entry beta_S for the high-AoA broadside direct-reentry phase (used only by equilibrium_glide_acton); Acton explicitly flags his fitted beta_S (7-10) as physically unreliable (his Newtonian flat-plate estimate, Eq.22, gives >100). Default guidance here is damped_glide (damped-phugoid, zeta 0.7) per user direction; dynamic_equilibrium_glide (gentle smooth capture) and equilibrium_glide_acton (three-phase pull-up) remain available.

Reentry mode: this object was characterised flying damped_glide; the shipped default is the neutral equilibrium_glide. Select the intended reentry mode in the Reentry-mode dropdown (the glide law is a flight-plan choice, not object hardware).
file:HTV-2.ro.json.source: Acton, 'Hypersonic Boost-Glide Weapons', Science & Global Security 23 (2015): 191-219, Table 3 (A-flight fit).

file:Hwasong-11.ro.json.name: Hwasong-11
file:Hwasong-11.ro.json.notes: Reentry mode: this object was characterised flying damped_glide, which is now its shipped default reentry plan. The glide law is a reentry-plan choice (still switchable on the sidebar strip), not object hardware.
file:Hwasong-11.ro.json.source: Screening estimate. DPRK Hwasong-11 (US designator KN-23) short-range ballistic missile, Iskander-M (9K720) analog: depressed/quasi-ballistic ~50 km apogee, ~450-690 km range, terminal pull-up maneuver, Mach ~6-7. Non-separating unitary airframe. No published aero/thermal fit - values are open-source order-of-magnitude estimates.

file:SWERVE.ro.json.name: SWERVE
file:SWERVE.ro.json.notes:
GEOMETRY sourced: 5.25-deg sphere-cone, nose_radius from published R_n/R_base=0.07 (R_base=L*tan(5.25)~0.238 m -> R_n~0.0167 m). base diameter 0.476 m is the CONE base; the ~0.61 m (2 ft) factsheet 'diameter' includes the wings. MASS 300 kg: reconstruction-fit value, not a documented one. No primary-source SWERVE mass has been found; the 450 kg program-class figure (SWERVE and the AHW glide body both cited ~450 kg) under-flew the flight-3 record in Thrusty (short of the ~1,180 km Kauai->Johnston range and the Mach-12 pull-out), while ~300 kg reproduces the range to ~10%, so 300 kg is adopted as the trajectory-fit mass pending a primary source. beta=24,733 kg/m2 = m/(Cd*A) holding the geometry-fixed Cd*A=0.0121 m2 (Cd~0.068 on the 0.178 m2 cone base, a realistic sharp-5.25-deg-cone hypersonic value); beta scales with mass, so it was rescaled from 37,100 (at 450 kg) by 300/450 to keep Cd*A constant. L/D 1.8 is the sustained-glide L/D set here (per user direction); the maneuvering flight-3 record (Williamson Fig. 20) shows a lower ~0.6 from the 'small wings', but the glide-trim value used for analysis is 1.8 (matching the AHW glide body of the same airframe). guidance=damped_glide models the maneuvering pull-up/push-over phugoid; the flight-3 loft (Kauai->Johnston, ~1,180 km, ~160 s, Mach ~12) and the exact Fig-20 AoA schedule are flown via the pitch program at run time, not baked into this RV. Per-location materials are DOCUMENTED (Murbach 1993 p.3): nose tip/leading edges = bare carbon-carbon (nose_tps_material=carbon_carbon), body = silica phenolic (body_tps_material=silica_phenolic). Legacy tps_material=carbon_ablator kept as the single-material fallback; it is the ORIGINAL ablative heat shield; the SWERVE->AHW claim is airframe reuse with an improved shield and higher glide L/D for AHW's much longer range -- AHW differs in TPS, glide L/D, and booster (STARS), not in basic airframe class.

Reentry mode: this object was characterised flying damped_glide; the shipped default is the neutral equilibrium_glide. Select the intended reentry mode in the Reentry-mode dropdown (the glide law is a flight-plan choice, not object hardware).
file:SWERVE.ro.json.source: Sandia Winged Energetic Re-entry Vehicle (SWERVE). Three flights 1979-1985 from the Kauai Test Facility on STRYPI boosters; flight 3 reentered near Johnston Island (~1,180 km). Spherically blunted 5.25-deg half-angle cone, 'a little over 100 in' long (~2.6 m), with small wings/elevons for lift and control, Mach 2-14 maneuvering. Nose-tip/heat-shield ablative. Flight-3 maneuver (Williamson, AIAA 92-3989, Fig. 20): ~-10 deg AoA push-over at 20 s/Mach 12, +10-15 deg pull-ups, ~4 deg control deflection; all flight data (Figs 20/23/24) end at ~160 s. (The AHW conical glide body is described as 'SWERVE with improved TPS'.)
